analyzed_vuln.description: Heap out-of-bounds read in DNS name decoding due to missing bounds check before reading the second byte of a compression pointer. In IDnsResource::decodeName(), `wordLength = encodedName[0]` is read safely, but when `(wordLength & 0xc0) == 0xc0`, the code computes `offsetInLayer` using `encodedName[1]` (line with `(0xFF & encodedName[1])`) after only checking `curOffsetInLayer + 2 > m_DataLen`. This check is vulnerable to size_t overflow when `curOffsetInLayer` is near SIZE_MAX (possible because pointer subtraction uses an out-of-range `encodedName` derived from malformed resource offsets), so the guard can be bypassed and `encodedName[1]` is read past packet end, causing the ASan 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: FuzzTarget feeds a malformed pcap packet that is parsed as UDP->DNS. In DnsLayer::parseResources(), attacker-controlled DNS counts/structure cause construction of a DnsQuery at an offset that can be at/near the end of the DNS buffer. IDnsResource constructor calls decodeName() on that offset. If the first byte has compression-pointer bits set (0xC0) but there is no second byte in bounds, decodeName still reads `encodedName[1]` due to the overflow-prone `curOffsetInLayer + 2 > m_DataLen` check, triggering OOB read.
